goal: Decide the CSV processing approach for csv-report, an internal tool that turns the weekly CSV export into a summary report and runs as a single script on an analyst's laptop.
question: Should csv-report keep its standard-library CSV processing or add a third-party data-handling dependency?
known_constraints: The tool is internal and runs as a single script on the analyst's laptop (README.md).
Weekly input file sizes have never been measured and vary a lot between weeks (README.md).
The current summary logic counts the rows of the export (process.py summarize).
The repository currently has no dependency manifest (verified by file listing).

environment.runtime: single script run locally on the analyst's laptop
environment.current_implementation: stdlib csv module; summarize() counts rows via a generator over csv.reader

evidence: The repository contains exactly README.md and process.py; there is no pyproject.toml, requirements.txt, or any other dependency manifest (file listing, 2026-10-02).

process.py imports only the standard-library csv module, and summarize() consumes csv.reader through a generator expression, so parsing is lazy and memory use does not grow with input size (process.py:1-12).
The process.py docstring says 'stdlib only today', which states the current implementation rather than a mandate (process.py:1).
Weekly CSV export sizes have never been measured and vary a lot between weeks (README.md:4-5).

pandas.read_csv reads the entire file into a single DataFrame by default regardless of low_memory; passing chunksize or iterator=True returns a TextFileReader for chunked iteration instead (official pandas documentation, https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/reference/api/pandas.read_csv.html, checked 2026-10-02).

alternatives.name: Keep Standard Library Only
alternatives.description: Continue using the Python standard-library csv module with plain-Python aggregation for the weekly summary report.
advantages: No dependency to install, pin, or upgrade on the analyst's laptop.
csv.reader yields rows lazily, so memory use does not grow with file size (process.py:11-12).
Runs on any Python installation with no environment setup steps.
disadvantages: Richer summaries such as grouping, filtering, or joins must be hand-written.
No higher-level data operations if report requirements grow.
assumptions: The weekly report remains a simple aggregate such as a row count or a few summary figures.

alternatives.name: Add a Data-Handling Dependency
alternatives.description: Introduce a third-party data-handling library (for example pandas or polars) and express the weekly summary as dataframe operations.
advantages: Grouping, filtering, and joins are available as library operations instead of custom code.
Established APIs reduce hand-written parsing and aggregation code as reports grow.
Chunked or streaming read modes exist for large files (pandas read_csv supports chunksize).
disadvantages: Requires an install step and version pinning on a laptop that currently has no dependency manifest.
pandas read_csv loads the entire file into one DataFrame by default, so memory use scales with file size unless chunked iteration is adopted.
Library upgrades and API changes become an ongoing maintenance concern for an internal tool.
assumptions: A pip/venv (or equivalent) install step is acceptable on the analyst's laptop.
Future reports will need operations beyond simple counting.

alternatives.name: Stay Standard Library with an Adoption Trigger
alternatives.description: Keep the standard-library implementation today and define an explicit trigger (for example measured file size or summary complexity) at which a data-handling dependency is adopted.
advantages: No dependency cost until a concrete need is demonstrated.
Turns the unmeasured file-size unknown (README.md) into a measured trigger condition.
Defers the library choice until actual requirements are known.
disadvantages: Requires someone to measure sizes and revisit the decision when the trigger fires.
Short-term richer reports still require hand-written aggregation.
assumptions: The team will maintain and act on the trigger condition.
Near-term report requirements stay close to the current row-count summary.

criteria.name: Fit for current workload
rubric: Poor fit: machinery far exceeds a row-count style summary
Acceptable fit: some extra machinery relative to current needs
Good fit: matches the current workload directly

criteria.name: Resilience to unknown, highly variable weekly file sizes
rubric: Memory use grows with file size by default and needs extra patterns to bound
Handles large files when additional configuration is applied
Memory use bounded by default regardless of file size

criteria.name: Capability headroom for richer reports
rubric: Richer analysis requires substantial hand-written code
Richer analysis requires moderate additional code
Rich aggregations available as ready-made library operations

criteria.name: Install, maintenance, and reproducibility burden on the analyst's laptop
rubric: Adds a heavyweight dependency with install, pinning, and upgrade overhead
Adds a small dependency with low upgrade churn
No new dependency; runs on any Python installation
